description: Change of use from C3 to C2 Children's Residential Care Home
decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a C3 dwellinghouse to a C2 children's home would result in the loss of an existing self-contained family dwelling. Whilst the proposed use would provide a form of specialist accommodation and the submitted Written Statement of Local Need is noted, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the loss of the existing family dwelling would be justified in the wider public interest or that this particular property would be suitable for the proposed use. The proposal would therefore conflict with the objective of safeguarding existing housing stock and would fail to demonstrate compliance with the policy requirements for residential care accommodation, contrary to Policies DMH 1 and DMH 8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies H8, H9 and H12 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed 24-hour staffed C2 children's home, involving up to four children, daytime and overnight staff, staff handovers, manager attendance and associated professional and visitor movements, would operate without causing undue noise, disturbance and general activity harmful to neighbouring occupiers. In the absence of a sufficiently detailed, site-specific and enforceable management framework, and in the absence of any noise assessment, acoustic report, sound insulation details or other mitigation measures, the proposal would fail to safeguard neighbouring residential amenity, contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies D3, D13 and D14 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed 24-hour staffed children's residential care home (Use Class C2) could operate without resulting in overspill parking, increased parking stress and consequent harm to highway safety and the free flow of traffic. The submitted Transport Assessment is based upon operational assumptions rather than site-specific survey evidence and fails to robustly assess the parking demand arising from staff shift changes, staff handovers, manager attendance, professional visits, inspections, family contact visits and other operational movements associated with the use. Furthermore, the precise needs profile of future residents, the eventual operator and the staffing requirements necessary to support future occupants remain unknown, creating further uncertainty regarding the likely transport impacts of the development.
